newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Press.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business Press.

text.p: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- SHELL SEEKS SUPPORT FOR RIGHTS RECORD

Anglo-Dutch oil group Shell has been briefing major institutional shareholders to ensure support from key investors to head off a resolution on its environmental and human rights record. The group is anticipating strong support following its decision to ask shareholders to reject criticism of its record. Opponents say Shell's decision has only served to increase support.
-- BP SEES NO CHANGES FOR NORTH SEA TAXES

British Petroleum believes Chancellor Gordon Brown will leave North Sea oil taxes untouched in his search for extra revenues. BP's chief executive John Browne said the group was not planning on any change. BP briefed government ministers when they were in opposition and it is hoping its efforts have paid off. Browne feels that the new government accepts that an increase in taxation will hit exploration and production.
-- DOMESTIC DEMAND BAILS OUT EXPORTS

According to surveys from the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply and the Confederation of British Industry and Business Strategies, domestic demand continued to rise in the run-up to the election for both retailers and other services businesses and manufacturers. However, manufacturers are continuing to struggle to hold growth in export markets.
THE TIMES
-- MARKETS WELCOME BROWN'S FIRST MOVES

Chancellor Gordon Brown has announced a quarter-point rise in interest rates to 6.25 per cent, along with radical reforms at the Bank of England. He surrendered the power to set interest rates to the Bank. The City reacted with enthusiasm with the stock market and the pound reaching new heights. Mortgage rates rose, with some building societies putting the cost by more than Brown's increase.
-- CAPITAL RADIO TO PAY 65 MILLION STG FOR VIRGIN RIVAL

Capital Radio has agreed to buy Virgin Radio for 65 million stg. Capital will fund the acquisition by issuing 11.9 million Capital shares to Richard Branson's Virgin Group. It is also taking on Virgin Radio's 22 million stg of debt, raising the total value of the deal to 87 million stg. Virgin will own 14 per cent of Capital and Branson will become a non-executive director.
-- UNILEVER DEFENDS ITS SOCIAL CHAPTER STANCE

Anglo-Dutch group Unilever has defended its pro-European stance against shareholder charges that it is too eager to comply with the EU's social chapter. Chairman Niall Fitzgerald said that British companies had no reason to fear the changes associated with Labour's plans to abandon the British opt-out. He told shareholders that the social chapter is being used as a proxy for all "undesirable Continental social habits".
THE GUARDIAN
-- CBI SOFTENS ITS OPPOSITION TO WINDFALL TAX

The Confederation of British Industry has said it would accept the windfall tax levy provided it was a one-off occurrence. CBI director general, Adair Turner, made it clear the employers' organisation had dropped its opposition to the tax and accepted that it would be imposed. Business will go along with it provided it was limited to a maximum of four billion stg and did no recur.
-- NORWICH UNION UNVEILS THE BIG WINDFALL DAY

Insurer Norwich Union has announced it will hand out 1.3 billion free shares to members when the company makes its debut on the stock market on June 16. Three million policyholders will receive windfalls of between 330 stg and 970 stg. Members will also be given the chance to subscribe for additional shares at a discount. Norwich Union expects the offer to raise 1.75 billion stg from private and institutional investors.
-- LLOYD'S DEFICIT AT 484 MILLION STG WITH NAMES DEBT HANGOVER

The Corporation of Lloyd's has announced a deficit of 484 million stg in 1996, compared to less than 14 million stg the previous year. It expects to recoup only half of the 600 million stg in debts owed by Names. Bob Hewes, finance director, admitted there were 1,300 writs outstanding, with hundreds of potential individual legal actions pending. Also, members are set to learn that their subscriptions and entrance fees will rise this year.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- DTI ROLE FOR LORD HOLLICK

Chief executive of United News and Media, Lord Hollick, is to be appointed special adviser to the new President of the Board of Trade, Margaret Beckett. Hollick's media group owns the Express titles and the Anglia and Meridian television franchises. Whitehall officials stressed that he would not be Beckett's only adviser as each member of the Cabinet is allowed to appoint two political advisers.
-- SETBACK FOR EUROTUNNEL'S ONE BILLION STG CLAIM

A five-man Anglo-French independent panel of experts has thrown out the bulk of Eurotunnel's one billion stg compensation claims against Transmanche Link, the consortium that built the Channel Tunnel, saying they were inadmissable. The ruling is a big blow to Eurotunnel and comes only weeks before it seeks approval from shareholders and banks for the re-financing of its 8.7 billion stg debt.
-- WHISKY PRODUCERS MAY LINK UP

One of Scotland's best known whisky distillers, William Grant & Sons, could be close to a link-up with Burn Stewart Distillers, the publicly quoted whisky group which has seen its shares slump following a dispute with its auditors. William Grant may take a stake of up to 49 per cent and the deal would involve Burn Stewart issuing new shares while the two groups would pool their own-label operations. BMC +44-171-377-1742
